briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Cheapest weed Michigan's ever seen — and the tax is now a campaign issue
briefs.top: Michigan prices hit a record low as the 24% wholesale tax squeezes an oversupplied market, and the tax is now front-and-center in the governor's race. Nationally, rescheduling grinds forward and psilocybin keeps racking up FDA momentum.

local.text: Rock-bottom prices: the average recreational ounce sold for $58 in June (down from $63 a year ago) — the cheapest weed has ever been in Michigan as the 24% tax squeezes an oversupplied market.
The tax is now political: Gov. Whitmer's road-funding plan leans on that 24% cannabis revenue — while the industry's lawsuit calls the tax unconstitutional and blames it for closures and layoffs.
GOP gov candidate John James is campaigning to eliminate or scale back the wholesale tax and crack down on hemp THC — putting cannabis squarely in the 2026 race.
The shakeout continues: 550+ dispensaries and growers have closed since 2019, 2025 posted the first-ever annual sales decline, and Ann Arbor's C3 Industries is cutting its Webberville grow + 62 jobs.
Enforcement watch: regulators fined Mint Cannabis in Coldwater $8,000 after its surveillance system was found offline for 34 days.

national.text: Rescheduling grinds on: a DEA judge ordered transcript corrections (final due this week) to the 2,470-page hearing record — the Schedule III process is moving, if slowly.
Already partly done: the DEA earlier downscheduled FDA-approved marijuana drugs and state-licensed medical marijuana to Schedule III, with the broader rescheduling still in an expedited hearing.
The hemp-THC ban still hits Nov 12 absent new law (~95% of hemp products go unlawful) — and the fight over regulating vs. banning THC drinks is heating up.

Psilocybin momentum: the FDA awarded national priority-review vouchers to psilocybin developers, and Compass' COMP360 hit two Phase 3 endpoints — pointing to a possible first approval by late 2026 or early 2027.
On the calendar: the FDA holds a public hearing on the therapeutic use of psychedelics on Sept 14.
